# Xintong Han

> Xintong Han is an Assistant Professor of Marketing in the Department of Marketing at the Faculty of Business Administration, Université Laval.

Canonical profile: https://han-xintong.github.io/
Official university profile: https://www.fsa.ulaval.ca/en/expert/xintong-han/
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7369-0506
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZbgMprUAAAAJ&hl=en
Email: xintong.han@fsa.ulaval.ca

## Research

Xintong Han studies quantitative marketing, digital platforms, platform economics, network economics, empirical industrial organization, structural econometrics, causal inference, and machine learning in econometrics.

## Selected peer-reviewed publications

- Digital revitalization or useless effort? Public e-commerce support and local specialty sales (2026). Xintong Han, Jan Victor Dee, Shaojia Wang & Kefan Chen. Journal of Development Economics, 179, 103665. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdeveco.2025.103665
  - Finding: Platform access increased online sales by 16.649% and decreased offline sales by 15.549%, while total sales remained broadly unchanged.
- Effectiveness of online education during the COVID-19 pandemic: Evidence from Chinese universities (2026). Xintong Han, Shijie Lu, Xin (Shane) Wang & Nan Cui. Production and Operations Management, 35(3), 978–994. https://doi.org/10.1177/10591478251361979
  - Finding: Online education increased mathematics scores by 8–11 points on a 100-point scale; effects varied with course type and lockdown policies.
- Nonlinear pricing in multidimensional context: An empirical analysis of energy consumption (2023). Xintong Han, Zimin Liu & Tong Wang. International Journal of Industrial Organization, 91, 103034. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijindorg.2023.103034
  - Finding: The structural estimates imply that a 1% price increase reduces total electricity demand by about 0.7%, with limited scope for further tariff optimization.
- Peer recognition, badge policies, and content contribution: An empirical study (2023). Xintong Han, Yushen Li & Tong Wang. Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, 214, 691–707. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jebo.2023.08.021
  - Finding: Peer votes encourage content creation, while identity-rich badges can constrain contributions through reputation and privacy concerns.

## Selected working papers

- Creator Platform Commission Design. With Pu Zhao, Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, and Bin Gu, Questrom School of Business, Boston University.
  - Summary: Examines how a platform’s move from a uniform 5% commission to 20%, followed by selective reductions to 5%, changed creator prices and content quality.
- Technology Adoption in Input-Output Networks. With Lei Xu · NET Institute Working Paper #18-05 · Bank of Canada Staff Working Paper 2019-51
  - Summary: Models Python 3 adoption when a software package’s adoption cost depends on whether its dependency packages support Python 3.
  - Source: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266251
  - Additional source: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2019/12/staff-working-paper-2019-51/
